featured_reviews.name: NITIN GARG
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience with Dr. Vijay Shetty when I recently took my wife for treatment. She was suffering from tenosynovitis, and he recommended a steroid injection based on his expertise. We agreed to the treatment after he assured us there would be no side effects. He informed us that the injection would cost Rs. 12,000.

When we received the bill, we found that the injection itself cost only Rs. 250, while Rs. 10,000 was charged for administering it. This felt very unfair and excessive.

A few weeks later, my wife noticed skin discoloration in the area where the injection was given. We went back to consult him, but he showed no concern about the side effect and simply advised us to see a dermatologist. He did not take any responsibility for the issue.

Before giving the injection, he never mentioned any possible side effects, nor did he suggest any solution for the discoloration afterward.

Overall, I found the doctor more focused on money than patient care. If he is charging such high fees, he should also show proper concern, transparency, and responsibility toward his patients.

I am a very conservative person when it comes to ANY invasive procedures. The injection was done purely on the basis of persistent symptoms, and you were given the option of waiting for some time. But you and your wife opted for the procedure, were informed of the entire process, and signed an informed consent form. Your wife clearly had the pain relief on her follow-up visit ( Nearly three months after the injection -07/04/2026) after the injection, but she had slight discoloration at the injection site. featured_reviews.name: Pranab Kamat
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a rather disappointing experience with Dr. Shetty. I had taken my mother to him as she was experiencing pain in her heel/ankle area. During the first visit, he promptly diagnosed it as osteoporosis, stating that he had seen several such cases before and appeared quite confident in his conclusion. He prescribed osteoporosis medication and advised a follow-up after a month if the pain persisted.

Unfortunately, my mother experienced no relief and the pain continued, so we revisited him after a month. This time, he asked for a DEXA scan to assess the severity of the osteoporosis and adjust the medication accordingly. The scan results, however, showed absolutely no signs of osteoporosis, with her T-score being in the positive range. When questioned about this, he gave an unconvincing explanation that osteoporosis can sometimes exist despite such results. This made us feel that he was unwilling to acknowledge his earlier misdiagnosis, which had been made hastily without proper examination. Our trust in his judgment was significantly affected.

We then consulted another well-regarded orthopedic surgeon, who, after proper examination and X-rays, completely ruled out osteoporosis and prescribed appropriate medication and treatment. My mother has since experienced considerable improvement and relief.

While Dr. Shetty may be a skilled doctor, I would sincerely urge him not to jump to conclusions or rely on overconfidence when diagnosing. Patients expect time, attention, and careful evaluation—especially when paying ₹2,500 for a consultation. On both visits, I felt he was in a rush to see as many patients as possible rather than giving each case due attention.

Additionally, I would caution patients to double-check the billing. For the follow-up, I was initially billed ₹2,500 again, and only when I questioned it was it corrected to ₹2,000.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend consulting Dr. Shetty.

Why Does One Knee Hurt More Than the Other?

Many patients have arthritis in both knees but experience much more pain on one side.

One knee may be more painful because of:

Worse alignment
Unequal muscle strength
Previous injury
Meniscus damage
Greater cartilage wear
More inflammation
Different loading while walking

Two knees may look similar on an X-ray but still behave differently. Pain is also influenced by muscle control, joint sensitivity, gait pattern, inflammation, and alignment.

This is why treatment should be planned separately for each knee. One side may respond to physiotherapy, activity modification, or injections, while the other may require more advanced management.

🦿 Complex Joint Replacement Surgeries – Restoring Function in Challenging Cases

Not all joint replacements are routine. Some cases require advanced planning, specialized implants, and precise surgical execution to restore mobility and quality of life.

🔹 Case 1 – Revision Total Hip Replacement

A previously well-done cemented hip replacement lasted 35 years 👏
The patient presented with implant loosening and bone loss (lysis).

🔧 Re-do surgery performed with: 
• Extended Trochanteric Osteotomy (ETO)
• Long uncemented stem
• Acetabular augments
• Multi-hole cup

🎯 Aim: Restore stability and address bone loss for long-term function


🔹 Case 2 – Complex Knee Replacement with Instability

Patient had gross knee deformity with ligament laxity.

🔧 Treatment: 
• Precise bone cuts
• Careful soft tissue balancing
• Knee replacement using primary implants with tibial stem extender

🎯 Aim: Achieve stability, alignment, and balanced knee function


🔹 Case 3 – Knee Replacement with Bone Loss

Severe deformity of the knees with tibial bone loss.

🔧 Reconstruction included: 
• Bone grafting with screws for the bony defect
• Knee replacement using stubby tibial stem extender

🎯 Aim: Rebuild bone support and ensure stable implant fixation

✨ Takeaway:
Complex joint problems need individualized solutions, advanced implants, and surgical precision to achieve the best outcomes.

💪 Restoring mobility. Rebuilding lives.

🦴 Cauda Equina Syndrome – A Spine Emergency

Cauda Equina Syndrome is a serious neurological condition caused by severe compression of the nerves at the lower end of the spinal cord. It requires urgent diagnosis and immediate treatment.

⚠️ Common symptoms may include:
• Weakness or complete paralysis of the ankle and toes 🦶
• Difficulty walking
• Loss of bladder or bowel control 🚨
• Numbness in the lower limbs
• Reduced or absent reflexes

🩺 Diagnosis is made primarily through clinical examination, while MRI is the gold standard investigation to identify the nerve compression.

⏳ This condition is a true surgical emergency.
Urgent spinal decompression surgery is often required to prevent permanent nerve damage and improve chances of recovery.

In this case, the patient was operated at 3 AM within 3 hours of presenting to us, highlighting the importance of timely intervention and coordinated emergency care.

🤝 Team work makes dream work — rapid diagnosis, anesthesia, OT staff, nursing care, and surgical teamwork all play a vital role in managing such emergencies. 💪🩺

🦵 Anterior Cruciate Ligament Tear

The Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) is one of the main stabilizing ligaments inside the knee joint. It connects the femur (thigh bone) to the tibia (shin bone) and helps control knee stability during walking, running, pivoting, and sports activities.

⚠️ ACL tears commonly occur due to:
• Sports injuries 🏃‍♂️
• Sudden twisting movements
• Pivoting or awkward landing after a jump
• Road traffic accidents 🚗💥

Patients may experience pain, swelling, instability, or a “giving way” sensation in the knee.

🔧 Treatment – ACL Reconstruction
ACL reconstruction is performed using a tendon graft. Common graft options include:
• Hamstring tendon
• Patellar tendon
• Peroneus Longus tendon

In this case, a Peroneus Longus graft was harvested and prepared for reconstruction.

🩻 The surgery was performed arthroscopically (keyhole surgery):
✅ Tibial and femoral tunnels were created
✅ The graft was passed and fixed securely
✅ Knee stability was restored

🎯 An equally important part of treatment is rehabilitation.
Proper physiotherapy and guided rehab are essential for:
✅ Regaining movement
✅ Restoring muscle strength
✅ Returning safely to sports and daily activities 💪🦵

🦴 Monteggia Variant Fracture 

A Monteggia fracture variant is a complex elbow injury involving a fracture of the proximal ulna (forearm bone near the elbow) along with a radial head fracture.

These injuries usually occur after a fall on an outstretched hand, road traffic accident, or other high-impact trauma 🚗💥

Patients commonly present with:
⚠️ Pain and swelling around the elbow
⚠️ Difficulty moving the elbow and forearm
⚠️ Reduced ability to lift or rotate the arm

🔧 Treatment:
• The ulna fracture was stabilized using an olecranon plate
• The radial head fracture was fixed with specialized headless screws to preserve the joint surface and movement

🎯 Goal of surgery:
✅ Restore normal elbow anatomy
✅ Achieve stable fixation
✅ Allow early guided rehabilitation

With anatomical reduction and proper rehabilitation, patients can regain good elbow movement and function 💪🦴

🦵 Tibial Plateau Fractures

A tibia plateau / condyle fracture involves the upper part of the tibia bone (shin bone) that forms the knee joint. These injuries affect the joint surface and need careful treatment to restore knee function.

📊 Classification (Schatzker): This case is a Type II (split-depressed) fracture, where the bone is both split and pushed down, affecting the smooth joint surface.

⚠️ How does it occur?
• Road traffic accidents 🚗💥  
• Sports injuries 🏃‍♂️
• Fall from height

🤕 Symptoms
• Pain and swelling around the knee  
• Difficulty or inability to bear weight  
• Reduced knee movement

Due to significant swelling, surgery is sometimes delayed for a few days to allow soft tissues to settle, ensuring safer outcomes and lesser wound complications 

🔧 Treatment: The fracture was fixed using an anterolateral raft plate, which helps support the joint surface, restore alignment, and provide stable fixation.

🎯 Goal: To achieve anatomical joint surface restoration and allow early, guided knee movement for better recovery 💪🦵

🦿 Complex Primary Total Knee Replacement - From Bed-Bound to Standing Again

Advanced Osteoarthritis of the knees can sometimes go beyond pain — causing severe deformity, bone loss, and complete loss of mobility for the patient.

Such cases require a complex surgical procedures using advanced implants with long stems, metal augments for bone loss, and meticulous soft-tissue balancing to restore alignment and function.

This patient had gross deformity of both legs and was barely able to stand or walk for past several months.

A Complex Primary Total Knee Replacement was performed using imported implants to restore alignment, balance, and stability.

✨ Most importantly:

The operated leg was realigned to a near-normal position, and the patient was able to stand again after 6 months 🙏🦿

The second knee is to be operated subsequently, and with proper rehabilitation, the patient is expected to walk with a near-normal gait.

Sometimes, timely surgery doesn’t just relieve pain — it restores dignity, independence, and hope 💙

⚠️ A gentle reminder: Don’t wait until arthritis becomes this severe. Early consultation and timely treatment can help avoid deformity and prolonged immobility.

🦴 Femur Shaft Fracture

A fracture of the shaft of the femur (thigh bone) is a serious injury, most commonly caused by high-energy trauma such as road traffic accidents 🚗💥.

At the scene or in the emergency setting, the limb is often stabilized using a Thomas traction splint to reduce pain and prevent further damage.

⚠️ These fractures can be associated with significant internal bleeding (up to 1–1.5 liters), so patients require urgent stabilization in the emergency room.

🔧 Definitive Treatment
Once the patient is stable, the fracture is treated with Closed Reduction and Internal Fixation using an Interlocking Femur Nail, which provides strong internal support and allows proper healing.

🎯 Goals of treatment:
✅ Stabilize the fracture
✅ Control pain and bleeding
✅ Allow early mobilization and recovery
Prompt and appropriate care is essential for a safe recovery and return to normal activity 💪🦴

🦴 Osteoporosis
Osteoporosis is a condition where bones become weak and brittle, increasing the risk of fractures even after minor falls or injuries.

❓ What causes it?
• Aging 👵👴
• Hormonal changes (especially after menopause)
• Low calcium and vitamin D intake 🥛☀️
• Lack of physical activity
• Certain medications like long term steroids

⚠️ What can happen?
Weak bones can lead to fragility fractures, commonly affecting:
• Hip 🦵
• Wrist ✋
• Spine (leading to back pain or height loss)

🩻 How is it diagnosed?
• Bone density scan (DEXA scan)
• X-rays (if fracture is suspected)

💊 Treatment:
• Calcium and Vitamin D supplements
• Special medications to strengthen bones
• Weight-bearing exercises
• Lifestyle changes (diet, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol)

🚶‍♂️ Fall Prevention Tips:
✔️ Keep floors dry and clutter-free
✔️ Use good lighting, especially at night 🌙
✔️ Wear non-slip footwear
✔️ Install grab bars/handrails
✔️ Regular check-ups for balance and bone health

Early diagnosis and treatment can help prevent fractures and maintain an active, independent life 💪🦴

🦴 Paediatric Both Bone Forearm Fracture

Fractures of both forearm bones (radius and ulna) are among the most common fractures in children, accounting for nearly 40% of all pediatric fractures.

They most often occur after a fall on an outstretched hand while playing. Children usually present with pain, swelling, and visible deformity of the forearm.🤸‍♂️

Diagnosis is confirmed with simple X-rays of the forearm.🩻

Most pediatric forearm fractures can be treated without surgery if the bones can be properly aligned and maintained with closed reduction and plaster casting.

However, surgery may be required if the fracture is significantly displaced or if the alignment cannot be maintained in the cast, especially in children nearing skeletal maturity.

In this case, closed reduction and casting could not maintain proper bone alignment, so the fracture was treated surgically using TENS (Titanium Elastic Nailing System) to stabilize the bones and allow proper healing.🔧

With appropriate treatment and rehabilitation, children usually recover excellent function and return to their normal activities 💪🦴

🦴 Pathological Hip Fracture in Advanced Cancer

In advanced stages of cancer, the disease can spread to the bones (bone metastasis), making them very weak and prone to fractures even after very minor trauma.

In this case, the patient had primary breast cancer with widespread metastasis, involving the brain, chest, spine, and multiple bones as detected on PET Scan (red areas on scan depict disease). The neck of the right femur (hip bone) fractured due to weakening from a metastatic lesion.

After careful evaluation and discussion with expert oncosurgeons and oncologist, the decision was made to proceed with palliative surgery. With high-risk informed consent of patient and the family, the hip joint was surgically replaced.
